topic: Rhi has just told the table that on Saturday she saw Gwen Price's husband Gareth having a very cosy dinner in a hotel in Ludlow with a woman who is not Gwen. Gwen is a customer and a friend of hers. Rhi hasn't said anything to anyone yet, and she's asking the table what she should do.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Gareth Price? He can't find his own way to Ludlow.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Hang on, how cosy is cosy? Because my brother-in-law takes his accountant to dinner and they look like they're on a honeymoon.

backchannels.after: look like they're on a honeymoon.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Cosy. Shared pudding cosy.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Right, so you do nothing. Nothing at all
T.full: Right, so you do nothing. Nothing at all. A man is allowed a sticky toffee pudding in Ludlow, it's practically a human right.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Wait, so your actual advice is she just bleeds Gwen's radiators every winter and says nowt? Forever?

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Hang on, did Gareth see you?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: No. Well. I don't think so.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: No, no, not forever. Just until he's stupid enough
T.full: No, no, not forever. Just until he's stupid enough to do it somewhere closer than Ludlow, which, knowing Gareth, is next week.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Oh he's not wrong about Gareth, bless him, but Gwen'll find out you knew, Rhi, and that's the bit she won't forgive.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Thank you. Until he's stupid enough.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Shared pudding. That's stupid enough.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Hang on, Rhi's asked the whole table and said about six words since. You've already decided
T.full: Hang on, Rhi's asked the whole table and said about six words since. You've already decided, haven't you?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Half. And I'm in her kitchen Thursday servicing the boiler, so I've got till then to sort my face out.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Can't prove a thing, mind, but his father went to Ludlow every Saturday for twenty years and never once came home with shopping.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Oh my God, so it's hereditary. Ludlow's the family business, they just pass it down.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: That's where I was going, that. Hugh, did his mom know?
T.full: That's where I was going, that. Hugh, did his mom know? Because if she did and kept her mouth shut, well...

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Who d'you think did his shopping?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: No. Who? Hugh. Who?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Nancy Probert. Had the wool shop by the bridge. Whole town knew bar his wife. Femi, you'd tell Gwen, would you?

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: See, Nancy Probert's my point. Half of Ludlow's seen that pudding, so Gwen's last to know unless someone tells her
T.full: See, Nancy Probert's my point. Half of Ludlow's seen that pudding, so Gwen's last to know unless someone tells her. So yeah. I would.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Lovely, so half of Ludlow's seen it, let one of them be the hero. Why's it got to be the woman with the spanner?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Oi. The woman with the spanner has been under Gwen's sink since her twins were in nappies, I know where she hides the Baileys, Danny. That's not a customer, that's, that's a mate.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Fine, a mate, I withdraw the spanner. But then you know her. So never mind what you should do, would Gwen want telling, or would she rather find out without you standing there?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Gwen? Gwen'd want telling. Gwen'd want the hotel, the table, the woman's coat
T.full: Gwen? Gwen'd want telling. Gwen'd want the hotel, the table, the woman's coat, and what the pudding was.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Go on then, what coat?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Camel. Long, belted, never been near a field. See, that's my problem, I'd do the coat before I'd do the kind bit.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Hang on, long, belted, camel. How long were you stood there looking at this coat
T.full: Hang on, long, belted, camel. How long were you stood there looking at this coat if Gareth definitely didn't see you?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: I'd ordered, Femi! What was I—

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: No, but that's it, Thursday, Gwen opens the door and you'll do the coat before the kind bit, I know you will.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Do it now, then. I'm Gwen.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Gwen, love. Sit down

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Sit down? In my own kitchen? You've never told me to sit down in fifteen years, Rhi, I'd know straight off it was Gareth.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Then don't go Thursday. You've eight of them working for you, send the one who can't read a face and wouldn't know a camel coat from a horse blanket.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Fifteen years it's Rhi, then this Thursday some lad she's never met turns up instead? Gwen'll know before he's got the cover off.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Has anyone thought Gwen might know already?
T.full: Has anyone thought Gwen might know already? Thursday she opens the door, and it's you getting handled gently over the boiler.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Oh God, and if she does know, would she even tell you, Rhi? Or are you suddenly just the woman who does the boiler?
